findings.claim: The unanchored `docs?` branch in the `docsOnly` regex at engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:174 matches any path merely starting with the substring "doc" (e.g. `docker-compose.yml`, `src/docker/build.ts`, `documented-api.ts`), misclassifying real source-code changes as documentation-only and skewing reviewer-roster selection in `/review-pr`.

parseRegisteredFacadeProgram discards parseRemediationStartInput/parseWaveGateStartInput/parseStandaloneStartInput's specific error message, collapsing every validation failure of an already-matched variant into a bare null
gitPaths and gitText never check spawnSync's result.error, so a failed process spawn (e.g. missing git binary) throws a generic fallback message instead of the actual spawn failure reason

No test directly pins that AGENT_CATALOG["architecture-tech-lead"].requiredSkill equals "deepen" specifically (as opposed to any other internally-consistent skill name), relying entirely on cross-file consistency checks rather than a golden value assertion

No test directly pins that `AGENT_CATALOG["architecture-tech-lead"].requiredSkill` equals `"deepen"` specifically (as opposed to any other internally-consistent skill name), relying entirely on cross-file consistency checks rather than a golden value assertion

RegisteredWaveGateProgram's `restart` and `orphanRecovery` fields are independently optional, so the type permits a registration with both recovery contexts set even though every constructor and the untrusted-input parser only ever populate one.

helpers.ts repeats the ad-hoc union `Readonly<{ ok: true; value: T }> | Readonly<{ ok: false; message: string }>` inline across many functions (e.g. parseStandaloneStartInput, parseWaveGateStartInput, parseRemediationStartInput, parsedAuthority, standaloneRetryEffectId) instead of a shared named generic, unlike PolicyResult<T>/ParseResult<T>/ProofParseResult<T> elsewhere in the codebase.

resolveAgentPolicy in model-profiles.ts is annotated to return PolicyResult<AgentPolicy> (Agent defaulted to string), discarding the LoomAgentName narrowing that AGENT_POLICIES and parseAgentName already establish, even though the resolved value's agent field is always a LoomAgentName.

skills/code-implementer/SKILL.md:11 tells the reader to use `/architecture-tech-lead` as a slash command, but no such command is registered — commands/ has no architecture-tech-lead.md, and skills/deepen/SKILL.md correctly refers to the same target without a leading slash as a Skill/Agent, not a command.

engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:357-366's doc comment for renderSpawnTask omits the optional `LOOM_REVIEW_CONTEXT: standalone` marker line the function actually prepends when `options.standalone` is true, and its claim that authority alone determines the task text ignores that `instruction` and `options.standalone` also shape the output.

engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:100's doc comment describes `CanonicalChangedPaths.unstaged` as paths "not represented by HEAD," but the tracked-unstaged subset (from `git diff --name-only`) is paths whose HEAD entry exists and only differs in content, so the phrase only accurately describes the untracked half of the union.

metadata() in engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts fuses pure scope classification (docsOnly, sourceOrTestChanged, newStructure, languages) with an I/O-bound additions fetch (trackedAdditions/untrackedAdditions spawning git), so the reviewer-auto-select classification cannot be unit-tested without a real git repo or subprocess mock.

The newStructure field in engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts is computed as a bare path-depth check (>=4 segments), not a genuine new-service/package/migration detector, so its name and the architecture-tech-lead auto-select documentation promise a semantic the implementation does not verify.

validateAgentPolicyCatalog (engine/src/core/model-profiles.ts:385-418) runs the same missing/duplicate/unexpected multiset-reconciliation logic twice — once for model profiles against LLM_PROFILE_IDS, once for agent policies against expectedAgents — differing only in message vocabulary ('unknown' vs 'unexpected'). Extracting a small reconcile(expected, actual, missingLabel, duplicateLabel, extraLabel) helper used by both blocks, preserving today's exact message text, removes the duplicated loop bodies without changing the function's signature, defaults, or return value.

parseRegisteredFacadeProgram (engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:415-456) rebuilds the same 5-element wave-gate key array ['schemaVersion','kind','input','taskIds','authorityDigest'] three times inside a nested ternary just to append one optional key name ('restart' or 'orphanRecovery'). Hoisting the shared array into a baseKeys constant and spreading it (waveKeys = hasRestart ? [...baseKeys,'restart'] : hasOrphanRecovery ? [...baseKeys,'orphanRecovery'] : baseKeys) removes the triplicated literal while validating the exact same key sets.

pi-extension-review-events.test.ts repeats the same env-restore idiom (if (previous === undefined) delete process.env.X; else process.env.X = previous;) inline at three separate sites — the afterAll block (lines 97-109, 7 variables), the runtime-skew test's finally block (lines 271-274), and the late-task-graph test's finally block (lines 827-828). A single module-scope restoreEnv(key, previous: string | undefined) helper used at all three call sites removes roughly 14 duplicated lines with no change to which env vars are restored or when.

entries.reasoning: Concrete trigger exists: `/(^|\/)(docs?|README)|\.(md|mdx|txt)$/.test('docker-compose.yml')` matches via `^` + `doc` (the `s` is optional and nothing anchors the end), so a scope of only `docker-compose.yml`/`docker/Dockerfile` (derived by `deriveChangedPaths` in `startStandaloneFacade`, /home/peterstorm/dev/claude-plugins/loom/engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/standalone.ts:26-35) yields docsOnly=true with sourceOrTestChanged=false, which passes the parse boundary at engine/src/core/standalone-review.ts:262 and then drops silent-failure-hunter (gated on `!metadata.docsOnly`, line 293) and adds comment-analyzer (line 298); for `.ts` paths like `src/docker/build.ts` the same match instead makes docsOnly && sourceOrTestChanged true and hard-fails the run at line 262-263, so every reproduction path ends in wrong behavior.

Reproducible from a registration whose variant is already matched but whose input is invalid, e.g. `schemaVersion:1,kind:'remediation',input:sourceRunsRoot:'',sourceRun:'x',supportPaths:[]`: helpers.ts:418-421 returns bare null, so `resumeOperation` (engine/src/handlers/helpers/orchestration.ts:715-726) falls through to the panel parser and reports the generic 'registered orchestration program is malformed' instead of parseRemediationStartInput's message, and an invalid-but-present wave-gate registration makes restartOperation (line 645-648) report 'restart currently requires a registered Wave Gate run' — a demonstrably wrong diagnostic for a run that IS a wave-gate run.

The intended meaning of docsOnly is stated explicitly in /home/peterstorm/dev/claude-plugins/loom/engine/src/core/standalone-review.ts:253-264 ('docs_only is by definition "no source or test file changed"') and :245-249 ('comment analysis is the only role that reads docs'), yet the regex at helpers.ts:174 has its first alternative unanchored at the end, so 'docker-compose.yml' or 'docker/entrypoint.sh' satisfy scope.every(...) and yield docsOnly=true (dropping silent-failure-hunter and adding comment-analyzer per selectStandaloneReviewers:293,298), while a scope of only 'src/docker/build.ts' produces the contradictory docsOnly && sourceOrTestChanged pair the parse boundary at :262 exists to reject; either outcome contradicts the documented intent, so I could not refute it.

My best refutation was that null is the deliberate 'shape did not match' discriminator contract needed by the resume fallback to parseRegisteredPanelProgram (orchestration.ts:715-726), but that only justifies null for unmatched shapes, not for the already-matched variants the finding names: once kind==='remediation'/'wave-gate' matched, the discarded message makes callers assert falsehoods ('restart currently requires a registered Wave Gate run' at orchestration.ts:646-647, 'this registered program does not accept user decisions' at :1163-1164) about a genuinely wave-gate-kinded but invalid registration, which contradicts the file's own stated design of typed, defect-naming diagnostics (durablePublicationDigest's 'corrupt' messages at helpers.ts:484-495 and the decodeReviewerTranscript docblock at :681-687).

The mis-set flag genuinely reaches consumers: `metadata()` (engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:174) feeds `reviewMetadata` straight into `standalonePackets` -> `selectStandaloneReviewers` (helpers.ts:248) and into `prepareFreshStandaloneReview` (standalone.ts:34-53), and no downstream guard catches the false positive for non-source paths — a scope of only `docker-compose.yml` (.yml is not in SOURCE_EXTENSIONS, so `sourceOrTestChanged` is false and the `docsOnly && sourceOrTestChanged` boundary check at core/standalone-review.ts:262 never fires) yields docsOnly=true, dropping silent-failure-hunter (line 293) and adding comment-analyzer (line 298); for `src/docker/build.ts` the same misclassification instead hard-aborts the run at that boundary check. The `every()` quantifier narrows how often it triggers but does not contain it.

The discarded message does reach an operator-facing surface: the bare null flows to orchestration.ts:715-726 ("registered orchestration program is malformed"), :853-857 (same), :645-647 ("restart currently requires a registered Wave Gate run") and :1162-1164 ("this registered program does not accept user decisions"), so a wave-gate/remediation registration that failed only its input validation is reported with a generic or actively wrong reason; the null cannot be defended as dispatch signalling for an already-matched variant either, since parseRegisteredPanelProgram only accepts kinds architecture/refutation and can never claim a `kind: "remediation"` record.

entries.reasoning: Concrete trigger exists: `/(^|\/)(docs?|README)|\.(md|mdx|txt)$/.test('docker-compose.yml')` matches via `^` + `doc` (the `s` is optional and nothing anchors the end), so a scope of only `docker-compose.yml`/`docker/Dockerfile` (derived by `deriveChangedPaths` in `startStandaloneFacade`, /home/peterstorm/dev/claude-plugins/loom/engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/standalone.ts:26-35) yields docsOnly=true with sourceOrTestChanged=false, which passes the parse boundary at engine/src/core/standalone-review.ts:262 and then drops silent-failure-hunter (gated on `!metadata.docsOnly`, line 293) and adds comment-analyzer (line 298); for `.ts` paths like `src/docker/build.ts` the same match instead makes docsOnly && sourceOrTestChanged true and hard-fails the run at line 262-263, so every reproduction path ends in wrong behavior.

Reproducible from a registration whose variant is already matched but whose input is invalid, e.g. `schemaVersion:1,kind:'remediation',input:sourceRunsRoot:'',sourceRun:'x',supportPaths:[]`: helpers.ts:418-421 returns bare null, so `resumeOperation` (engine/src/handlers/helpers/orchestration.ts:715-726) falls through to the panel parser and reports the generic 'registered orchestration program is malformed' instead of parseRemediationStartInput's message, and an invalid-but-present wave-gate registration makes restartOperation (line 645-648) report 'restart currently requires a registered Wave Gate run' — a demonstrably wrong diagnostic for a run that IS a wave-gate run.

The intended meaning of docsOnly is stated explicitly in /home/peterstorm/dev/claude-plugins/loom/engine/src/core/standalone-review.ts:253-264 ('docs_only is by definition "no source or test file changed"') and :245-249 ('comment analysis is the only role that reads docs'), yet the regex at helpers.ts:174 has its first alternative unanchored at the end, so 'docker-compose.yml' or 'docker/entrypoint.sh' satisfy scope.every(...) and yield docsOnly=true (dropping silent-failure-hunter and adding comment-analyzer per selectStandaloneReviewers:293,298), while a scope of only 'src/docker/build.ts' produces the contradictory docsOnly && sourceOrTestChanged pair the parse boundary at :262 exists to reject; either outcome contradicts the documented intent, so I could not refute it.

My best refutation was that null is the deliberate 'shape did not match' discriminator contract needed by the resume fallback to parseRegisteredPanelProgram (orchestration.ts:715-726), but that only justifies null for unmatched shapes, not for the already-matched variants the finding names: once kind==='remediation'/'wave-gate' matched, the discarded message makes callers assert falsehoods ('restart currently requires a registered Wave Gate run' at orchestration.ts:646-647, 'this registered program does not accept user decisions' at :1163-1164) about a genuinely wave-gate-kinded but invalid registration, which contradicts the file's own stated design of typed, defect-naming diagnostics (durablePublicationDigest's 'corrupt' messages at helpers.ts:484-495 and the decodeReviewerTranscript docblock at :681-687).

The mis-set flag genuinely reaches consumers: `metadata()` (engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:174) feeds `reviewMetadata` straight into `standalonePackets` -> `selectStandaloneReviewers` (helpers.ts:248) and into `prepareFreshStandaloneReview` (standalone.ts:34-53), and no downstream guard catches the false positive for non-source paths — a scope of only `docker-compose.yml` (.yml is not in SOURCE_EXTENSIONS, so `sourceOrTestChanged` is false and the `docsOnly && sourceOrTestChanged` boundary check at core/standalone-review.ts:262 never fires) yields docsOnly=true, dropping silent-failure-hunter (line 293) and adding comment-analyzer (line 298); for `src/docker/build.ts` the same misclassification instead hard-aborts the run at that boundary check. The `every()` quantifier narrows how often it triggers but does not contain it.

The discarded message does reach an operator-facing surface: the bare null flows to orchestration.ts:715-726 ("registered orchestration program is malformed"), :853-857 (same), :645-647 ("restart currently requires a registered Wave Gate run") and :1162-1164 ("this registered program does not accept user decisions"), so a wave-gate/remediation registration that failed only its input validation is reported with a generic or actively wrong reason; the null cannot be defended as dispatch signalling for an already-matched variant either, since parseRegisteredPanelProgram only accepts kinds architecture/refutation and can never claim a `kind: "remediation"` record.

advisory_findings.claim: gitPaths and gitText never check spawnSync's result.error, so a failed process spawn (e.g. missing git binary) throws a generic fallback message instead of the actual spawn failure reason

No test directly pins that AGENT_CATALOG["architecture-tech-lead"].requiredSkill equals "deepen" specifically (as opposed to any other internally-consistent skill name), relying entirely on cross-file consistency checks rather than a golden value assertion

No test directly pins that `AGENT_CATALOG["architecture-tech-lead"].requiredSkill` equals `"deepen"` specifically (as opposed to any other internally-consistent skill name), relying entirely on cross-file consistency checks rather than a golden value assertion

RegisteredWaveGateProgram's `restart` and `orphanRecovery` fields are independently optional, so the type permits a registration with both recovery contexts set even though every constructor and the untrusted-input parser only ever populate one.

helpers.ts repeats the ad-hoc union `Readonly<{ ok: true; value: T }> | Readonly<{ ok: false; message: string }>` inline across many functions (e.g. parseStandaloneStartInput, parseWaveGateStartInput, parseRemediationStartInput, parsedAuthority, standaloneRetryEffectId) instead of a shared named generic, unlike PolicyResult<T>/ParseResult<T>/ProofParseResult<T> elsewhere in the codebase.

resolveAgentPolicy in model-profiles.ts is annotated to return PolicyResult<AgentPolicy> (Agent defaulted to string), discarding the LoomAgentName narrowing that AGENT_POLICIES and parseAgentName already establish, even though the resolved value's agent field is always a LoomAgentName.

skills/code-implementer/SKILL.md:11 tells the reader to use `/architecture-tech-lead` as a slash command, but no such command is registered — commands/ has no architecture-tech-lead.md, and skills/deepen/SKILL.md correctly refers to the same target without a leading slash as a Skill/Agent, not a command.

engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:357-366's doc comment for renderSpawnTask omits the optional `LOOM_REVIEW_CONTEXT: standalone` marker line the function actually prepends when `options.standalone` is true, and its claim that authority alone determines the task text ignores that `instruction` and `options.standalone` also shape the output.

engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:100's doc comment describes `CanonicalChangedPaths.unstaged` as paths "not represented by HEAD," but the tracked-unstaged subset (from `git diff --name-only`) is paths whose HEAD entry exists and only differs in content, so the phrase only accurately describes the untracked half of the union.

metadata() in engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts fuses pure scope classification (docsOnly, sourceOrTestChanged, newStructure, languages) with an I/O-bound additions fetch (trackedAdditions/untrackedAdditions spawning git), so the reviewer-auto-select classification cannot be unit-tested without a real git repo or subprocess mock.

The newStructure field in engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts is computed as a bare path-depth check (>=4 segments), not a genuine new-service/package/migration detector, so its name and the architecture-tech-lead auto-select documentation promise a semantic the implementation does not verify.

validateAgentPolicyCatalog (engine/src/core/model-profiles.ts:385-418) runs the same missing/duplicate/unexpected multiset-reconciliation logic twice — once for model profiles against LLM_PROFILE_IDS, once for agent policies against expectedAgents — differing only in message vocabulary ('unknown' vs 'unexpected'). Extracting a small reconcile(expected, actual, missingLabel, duplicateLabel, extraLabel) helper used by both blocks, preserving today's exact message text, removes the duplicated loop bodies without changing the function's signature, defaults, or return value.

parseRegisteredFacadeProgram (engine/src/handlers/helpers/programs/helpers.ts:415-456) rebuilds the same 5-element wave-gate key array ['schemaVersion','kind','input','taskIds','authorityDigest'] three times inside a nested ternary just to append one optional key name ('restart' or 'orphanRecovery'). Hoisting the shared array into a baseKeys constant and spreading it (waveKeys = hasRestart ? [...baseKeys,'restart'] : hasOrphanRecovery ? [...baseKeys,'orphanRecovery'] : baseKeys) removes the triplicated literal while validating the exact same key sets.

pi-extension-review-events.test.ts repeats the same env-restore idiom (if (previous === undefined) delete process.env.X; else process.env.X = previous;) inline at three separate sites — the afterAll block (lines 97-109, 7 variables), the runtime-skew test's finally block (lines 271-274), and the late-task-graph test's finally block (lines 827-828). A single module-scope restoreEnv(key, previous: string | undefined) helper used at all three call sites removes roughly 14 duplicated lines with no change to which env vars are restored or when.
